mission_1.search: On the open map, BFS and A* both found a path of 13.5 m. BFS expanded 928 nodes, while A* expanded 700, so A* examined 228 fewer nodes. My BFS implementation uses a FIFO deque and marks cells as discovered when adding them. This explores cells in increasing numbers of steps from the start and finds a shortest path on this unit cost grid. My A* implementation uses a heap ordered by g + h, where g is the cost so far and h is the Manhattan distance to the goal. This heuristic directs the search toward promising cells while preserving shortest path optimality. A* therefore found an equally short route with fewer expansions. However, it was slightly slower in this run, showing that fewer expansions do not necessarily mean lower measured planning time.
mission_1.failure:
On the constrained map, BFS succeeded with a 24.5 m path and 848 expansions. DFS also succeeded, but its path was 104.0 m despite expanding fewer nodes: 524. My DFS implementation uses a LIFO stack, so it follows deeper branches rather than exploring by increasing distance. It prevents cycles but does not guarantee a shortest path.

IDDFS reached resource_limit after its expansion counter reached 250,001, exceeding the 250,000 expansion budget. My implementation repeats depth limited DFS with increasing limits, resets its path records each time, and prevents cycles along the current path. This repeats substantial work, which explains why it exhausted the budget. Its recorded path length of 0.0 does not represent a successful zero length route.

For the unreachable case, all four methods—BFS, DFS, IDDFS and A*—returned no_path. BFS, DFS and A* each expanded 9 nodes, while IDDFS expanded 231 because of repeated searches. no_path means the search exhausted the possibilities without finding a route. resource_limit means it stopped before finishing because it exceeded a work or time limit. It does not prove that a route is impossible.

I used ChatGPT to help implement and explain the four searches. I saved the implementation and ran the full evaluation in the lab guide. The results confirmed that all four methods succeeded on the diagnostic corridor, BFS and A* found equal shortest path lengths on the open and constrained maps, and all four returned no_path for the unreachable case.
